title: Split scenario specs and modernize load harness
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Current load/perf scenario definitions live in scattered YAML blobs, some embedded in the legacy node-based runner and others referenced by the eval pipeline. This creates duplication, brittle test behavior, and makes it hard to ensure parity between perf regression runs and ad-hoc load tests. This ticket splits scenario/spec responsibilities and modernizes the harness: introduce a single canonical scenario schema (JSON Schema v1), build a lightweight converter for existing YAML files, containerize the k6-based runner, and wire runs into CI with artifacts saved to S3 and metadata sent to the perf dashboard. The goal is developer ergonomics (single source-of-truth), reproducibility for regression jobs, and a smaller maintenance surface for future dependency upgrades.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical scenario JSON schema v1 committed to perf-infra repo and documented in Confluence
All legacy YAML scenarios converted with converter script; converter added to repo and covered by unit tests
Containerized k6 runner image built and published to ghcr.redwood-inference.com with tags for sha and semver
CI workflow (GitHub Actions) matrix runs perf regression against stable seeds and uploads artifacts to S3 under perf-artifacts/{run_id}
Perf dashboard shows linked run metadata (commit, scenario name, target model) and artifacts are downloadable
No user-facing API changes and smoke run against staging passes with <=10% deviation from baseline for the canonical 1k-token scenario
tasks: Draft JSON Schema v1 for scenarios (parameters, phases, clients, load profile, warmup)
Implement yaml->json converter (node script) and tests
Containerize k6 runner and bake common shims for env vars / secrets
Create GitHub Actions workflow to produce matrixed runs and upload artifacts to S3
Integrate run metadata posting to perf dashboard (via existing perf-ingest endpoint)
Backfill 10 highest-value scenarios from legacy YAML into canonical JSON
Update README + Confluence doc with migration steps and example scenarios
Add post-run validation step to CI that checks for large regressions and opens ENG- tickets on failure
progress_updates: 2026-02-07: Initial schema draft completed; reviewed with Leah Gomez (PM) — accepted with small naming tweaks.
2026-02-15: Prototype yaml->json converter implemented; converted 3 production scenarios for validation. Observed minor missing fields in YAML variants (client tags).
2026-02-22: Decided to containerize k6 instead of switching to a different runner to limit scope. Trade-off: immediate portability vs longer-term feature roadmap to evaluate Vegeta/Gatling.
2026-02-28: First GH Actions workflow pushed to branch feature/eng/ENG-11721-ci-matrix. Workflow runs but S3 upload auth needs a secrets policy update.
2026-03-04: Security approved lightweight S3 role for perf-artifacts with one-week lifecycle. Updated workflow to use role. Run metadata now posts to perf-ingest v2.
2026-03-10: Converted 10 scenarios, container image built and pushed to ghcr. Open PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-infra/pull/421 (needs eng review + QA smoke)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Divergence between converted scenarios and original behavior -> Mitigation: add back-to-back validation runs comparing legacy and converted outputs for top scenarios
Risk: CI matrix increases billable infra spend -> Mitigation: add cost-aware gating and run heavy scenarios on schedule (nightly) while keeping fast smoke for PRs
Risk: Secret/credentials leakage in artifacts -> Mitigation: strip envs and redact sensitive fields before uploading; security reviewed role
Risk: Dashboard ingest schema mismatch -> Mitigation: send compatibility shim and include raw metadata blob in artifacts for debugging
notes: Follow-up: schedule a 2-hour pairing session to onboard two component teams to the schema (week of 2026-03-15)
Consider future work: add canonical seed management so regression runs are fully deterministic across infra upgrades
We should track infra cost delta in Console (per-run cost metric) for the first 4 weeks post-rollout
